extracted.intended_audience: International Preliminary Examining Authorities (IPEAs), international/search examiners, patent office managers responsible for PCT processing and quality
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and quality-management criteria for International Preliminary Examining Authorities conducting PCT international preliminary examination and search (including treatment of amendments, new matter, translations, QMS requirements, and clerical procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supersession of replacement sheets (Rule 70.16(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a first replacement sheet was acceptable but a later replacement sheet for the same numbered sheet contains subject matter going beyond the original disclosure, the later replacement sheet supersedes the earlier one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both the superseding and the superseded replacement sheets are attached to the international preliminary examination report with accompanying letters as required under Rule 70.16(a), to ensure elected Offices receive both the version forming the basis of the report and later amendments not considered for that purpose. The superseded sheet is marked 'SUPERSEDED REPLACEMENT SHEET (RULE 70.16(b))'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption on translations when assessing amendments (20.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment is filed in a language different from the language of the application as filed, the examiner should assume, absent evidence to the contrary, that the original translation used for publication or required under Rule 55.2 conforms with the original language text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assumption is used for determining whether the amendment goes beyond the disclosure of the application as filed when language differences are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: When an amendment introduces subject matter beyond the application as filed (new matter) (20.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment is unacceptable as new matter if the overall change (addition, alteration or excision) results in the skilled person being presented with information not expressly or inherently presented in the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inherency requires that the missing descriptive matter is necessarily present and would be recognized by persons of ordinary skill; inherency cannot be based on probabilities or possibilities. Mere possibility that something could result is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of amendments likely to introduce new subject matter (20.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly adding matter not previously mentioned (or only implied) can introduce new subject matter; e.g., stating that a further ingredient might be added to a rubber composition, or specifying a particular kind of resilient support (like helical springs) where none was originally disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such additions should normally be regarded as going beyond the original disclosure unless other criteria (see 20.14) are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible clarifications when feature is well known (20.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment adding a specific feature may be permissible if the applicant convincingly shows that, in the context of the claimed invention, the feature would be so well known to the person skilled in the art that its introduction is an obvious clarification and does not extend the application content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: specification of helical springs is permissible if drawings interpreted by the skilled person show helical springs or if it is natural practice to use helical springs for the mounting in question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarifying an effect of a disclosed feature (20.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a technical feature was clearly disclosed but its effect was not mentioned or fully mentioned, later clarification of that effect in the description may be acceptable provided it can be deduced without difficulty by a person skilled in the art from the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such clarifications might not contravene Article 34(2)(b) if readily deducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction of further examples (20.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adding further examples (e.g., additional chemical examples) should be treated with caution because prima facie any further illustrative example may extend the disclosure beyond the originally filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine carefully whether the new example adds subject matter not originally disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of later-filed examples/statements as evidence (20.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Later-filed examples or statements (even if not allowed into the application) may be considered by the examiner as evidence supporting allowability of claims, e.g., showing that the invention can be readily applied across the claimed field or supporting inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When such evidence is used to support a positive conclusion on inventive step or other allowability aspects, the examiner should mention this evidence in the international preliminary examination report (see paragraphs 5.52, 5.53, 13.15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements of the technical problem must be deducible (20.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment to or insertion of a statement of the technical problem solved by the invention must meet Article 34(2)(b); revising the stated problem to emphasize an effect (after claim restriction) is permissible only if that effect is deducible without difficulty by a person skilled in the art from the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See paragraphs 20.15 and 20.16 regarding deducibility and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alteration or excision that changes disclosed embodiments may introduce new matter (20.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Altering or omitting features of an originally disclosed example may result in an amended example that is materially different and thus introduce new subject matter (e.g., changing an outer layer material in a multi-layer panel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the amended example depicts a panel or product that differs substantially from the original disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding claim-disclosed subject matter into description and support issues (20.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is permissible to amend the description to include subject matter that was disclosed in a claim of the application as filed; however, the amended description must still provide the required support for the claims and any contradictions must be resolved by amending claims or description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special care where adding negative limitations to overcome prior art as this may raise lack-of-support issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for claim amendments and handling of negative limitations/disclaimers (20.21 and Appendix A20.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment to claims or addition of new claims must be supported by the description as originally filed; each claim limitation must be explicitly or inherently supported. Negative limitations, exclusions, or disclaimers must be examined for new matter issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divergent practices exist: (A20.21[1]) A negative limitation raises a new matter issue if the excluded subject matter lacks support in the application as filed. (A20.21[2]) A negative limitation or disclaimer with no basis in the application as filed may be permissible to overcome accidental anticipation or to exclude parts for reasons other than novelty (e.g., lack of industrial applicability or insufficient disclosure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to translated applications and invitations to provide translations (20.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner determines an erroneous translation has been published or furnished under Rule 55.2/55.3, or that an amendment is not in the language of examination, the examiner may invite the applicant to provide or correct the translation to conform with the filed/published language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant fails to supply the translation within the time limit set, the amendment is not taken into account for purposes of the international preliminary examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to establish and maintain a Quality Management System (QMS) (Chapter 21 intro & 21.02-21.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each International Searching and Preliminary Examining Authority shall establish and maintain a QMS which complies with stated requirements and serves as a model for the Authority's individual quality scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The QMS must address leadership and policy; risk-based practices; resources; management of administrative workload; quality assurance; communication; documentation; search process documentation; and additional provisions including internal review and reporting arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership and policy responsibilities (21.04-21.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Top management is responsible for developing and implementing the QMS, establishing a quality policy, specifying responsibilities (documented in an organizational chart), conducting management reviews, ensuring availability of resources, and communicating the importance of meeting treaty/regulatory requirements and the QMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Top management or delegated officers should regularly review quality objectives, promote practices to address risks/opportunities, and ensure compatibility of the QMS with these Guidelines and continual improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk-based practices (21.11-21.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Authority should establish risk-based practices to identify factors that could cause operational processes or the QMS to deviate from requirements, implement preventive controls, and make use of opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested components: (i) understand the Authority's context and interested parties' needs; (ii) identify risks/opportunities as a planning basis; (iii) plan and implement actions to address risks/opportunities; (iv) check effectiveness of actions taken; (v) continuously update risks/opportunities. Formal documented risk-management processes are not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources: human, material, training and oversight (21.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Authority should have sufficient infrastructure to handle workload and comply with QMS requirements, including adequate human resources, administrative staff, equipment, documentation, training programs, and systems to monitor resource needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific expectations: (i) sufficient technically qualified staff for required fields; (ii) trained administrative staff to support processes; (iii) appropriate IT hardware/software; (iv) access to minimum documentation (Rule 34); (v) comprehensive up-to-date instructions for staff; (vi) effective training/development programs; (vii) continuous resource monitoring system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management of administrative workload (21.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Authority should have minimum practices/procedures for handling search/examination requests and related functions (data-entry, classification), including mechanisms to control timely issuance of reports and manage fluctuations and backlog.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include effective control mechanisms for timely issue of reports to a quality standard and control mechanisms for demand/backlog management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance procedures (21.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Authority shall have procedures ensuring timely issuance of high-quality search and examination reports, including internal quality assurance, measurement and data collection systems, and verification of effectiveness of corrective actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures may include internal self-assessment, verification/validation and monitoring for compliance with the Guidelines, measurement/collection/reporting systems to ensure continuous improvement, and checklists for pre-issue verification or post-issue monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication: inter-authority, with users, WIPO and Offices (21.18-21.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorities must provide effective communication with other Authorities to share best practices and prompt feedback, nominate a quality contact person, and have systems to communicate with users (esp. unrepresented applicants) including complaint handling and user-satisfaction monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communication to users should include: (i) a system for handling complaints and corrective/preventative actions with feedback to users; (ii) procedures to monitor user satisfaction and meet legitimate expectations; (iii) clear guidance and information about the search/examination process (e.g., on websites). Authorities should publicize their quality goals. Authorities shall also provide effective communication with the International Bureau and designated/elected Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of the QMS and processes (21.22-21.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authority's QMS must be clearly described and implemented so all processes/products/services can be monitored, controlled and checked for conformity. The Authority shall provide a reference documenting procedures affecting quality and indicate where instructions are found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content to document includes: quality policy and commitment, scope of QMS (and justifications for exclusions), organizational structure and responsibilities, documented processes (receipt, classification, distribution, search, examination, publication, support), resources available, and descriptions of interactions between processes/procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records to maintain (21.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Authority should maintain records including definitions of stored documents, results of management review, training/skills/experience records, evidence of conformity, results of product requirement reviews, search/examination process records for each application, traceable work data, QMS audit records, and records of corrective/preventative actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also include records of actions taken regarding non-conforming products and examples of corrections, and search process documentation as per Section 8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search process documentation (21.26(i)-(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: For internal purposes each Authority should document its search process, including the databases consulted (patent and non-patent), keywords and combinations used, languages of search, classes/class combinations searched (IPC or equivalent), and a listing of all search statements used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation is primarily for internal use to enable traceability and reproducibility of the search strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of special search cases (21.26(vi)-(viii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorities should document special cases internally such as limitations of search and justification, lack of clarity of the claims, and lack of unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record rationale for any limitations and noteworthy issues encountered during search/examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal review arrangements (21.27-21.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Authority shall establish internal review arrangements to determine alignment with the QMS model and compliance with QMS requirements and the Guidelines; reviews should be objective, transparent and undertaken at least once a year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested input to reviews: (i) conformity with QMS and Guidelines, (ii) corrective/preventative actions taken, (iii) follow-up actions from previous reviews, (iv) QMS/process effectiveness, (v) feedback from customers (designated/elected Offices and applicants), (vi) recommendations for improvement. Authorities shall set up processes for monitoring, recording and measuring compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting arrangements (initial and annual reports) (21.31-21.32)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorities shall submit an initial report to the Meeting of International Authorities under the PCT describing QMS implementation and then prepare annual reports identifying lessons learned, actions taken, and recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports submitted by Authorities shall be made available by the International Bureau on WIPO's website to help identify and disseminate best practices among Authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt of the demand (22.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Preliminary Examining Authority normally receives the demand for international preliminary examination directly from the applicant, but may receive it from the International Bureau, a Receiving Office, an International Searching Authority or a non-competent IPEA under Rule 59.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural handling depends on source of the demand (direct applicant or transmitted by other Offices/Authorities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of competent IPEA and marking/transmission of demand (22.02-22.05)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a demand, the IPEA checks whether it is competent to receive the demand. If competent, it proceeds with review; if not, it indelibly marks the actual date of receipt and transmits the demand with accompanying documents to the International Bureau for further handling and notifies the applicant (using prescribed forms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a non-competent IPEA chooses to transmit directly to a competent IPEA, special forms are used (PCT/IPEA/436, PCT/RO/153, PCT/ISA/234); refunds of fees paid are made to the applicant by the non-competent body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling multiple competent IPEAs — invitation to applicant to choose (22.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more IPEAs are competent, the non-competent transmitting body must invite the applicant to indicate to which competent IPEA the demand should be transmitted within the applicable time limit; if the applicant responds, the demand is transmitted to the specified competent IPEA; if not, the demand is considered not submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time limits: 3 months from transmittal of ISR and written opinion, or 22 months from priority date, or 15 days from date of invitation, whichever is later. Prescribed forms (e.g., PCT/IPEA/442, PCT/IPEA/444) are used to notify the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification checks of the international application and correction procedure (22.06)
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA checks that the international application can be identified (applicant name/address, title, filing date, application number). If identification is deficient, the IPEA invites the applicant to submit corrections; if corrections are timely, the demand is considered received on the date the IPEA receives corrections; otherwise the demand is considered not submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form PCT/IPEA/404 to invite corrections and Form PCT/IPEA/407 to declare a demand not submitted if corrections are not made in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's entitlement to file a demand (residency/nationality rules) (22.07-22.09)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant is entitled to file a demand if resident or national of a Contracting State bound by Chapter II and the international application was filed with a receiving Office of (or acting for) such a State. If multiple applicants exist, it suffices that at least one applicant meets this requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If none of the applicants has the right, the demand is considered not submitted. Special timing notifications may be necessary where little time remains before expiration of 19 months from priority date for national phase entry in certain States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in applicant — entitlement verification (22.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant named on the demand differs from that on the request, the IPEA must check that the new applicant is entitled to make the demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify residency/nationality and other entitlement criteria as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of States by filing the demand (22.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a demand constitutes the election of all Contracting States which are designated and are bound by Chapter II of the Treaty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an automatic effect of filing a demand; check the list of Contracting States bound by Chapter II relevant to the filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check of particulars affecting date of receipt and defect correction (22.12-22.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: After checking particulars affecting the date of receipt and making a positive determination, the actual filing date is marked as date of receipt. If the demand form/computer print-out used does not comply with Administrative Instructions sections, the procedure for correcting defects applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IPEA notifies the applicant using the prescribed form (e.g., PCT/IPEA/402) of the date of receipt or of defects to be corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness check of the demand (Rule 54bis) and national-law incompatibility check (22.14-22.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA checks that the demand is filed within the applicable time limit (3 months from transmittal of ISR/written opinion or 22 months from priority date, whichever is later). If late, the demand is considered not submitted. Additionally, where a designated State's national law remains incompatible with a modified time limit, the IPEA checks whether the demand was received within 19 months from the priority date for that State and notifies the applicant accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If timely, notify applicant (Form PCT/IPEA/402); if not, issue declaration (Form PCT/IPEA/407) and notify the International Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing the IPEA file and document transmittal from the International Bureau (22.16-22.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of the demand, the IPEA establishes its file. If not part of the same national Office as the ISA or RO, the International Bureau will provide copies of the international application (or published application), the ISR, and the written opinion to the IPEA upon request. Copies of amendments under Article 19 and accompanying statements will be supplied unless submitted with the demand or reversed by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IPEA may collect cited documents from its own files or order them from the ISA; the IB transmits the written opinion promptly when available.
